key_insight: Exact dedup misses near-duplicates. bf16 full fine-tunes with ~1e-3 relative weight change leave many weights bit-identical, so lossless XOR deltas against a reference page compress well.
killer_doubt: A P-page read costs two DRAM reads (reference plus delta), and a write to a reference forces its dependents to re-encode. Realistic gain over KSM plus compression: ~1.2-2x.
decisive_experiment: Snapshot memory on 20 multi-tenant and model-serving hosts. Offline, measure capacity after KSM plus zstd, then after MinHash-chosen XOR deltas (<$50k). Advance only if the deltas add >=1.5x.
prior_art: Difference Engine (OSDI 2008), sub-page patching of similar pages; Thesaurus (ASPLOS 2020), LSH-clustered base+delta lines; ZipNN fine-tune XOR deltas. From memory.

key_insight: The per-variant arithmetic holds: a 1-bit sign delta plus per-row scales is ~1/16 of bf16, a 16x saving per variant against a full copy.
killer_doubt: The headline is ~6x wrong: 100 one-bit deltas add 6.25 base-sizes, so the total is ~7.3x the base, not 1.1x. BitDelta already ships the fused kernel.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Reproduce BitDelta serving 100 Llama-3-8B variants on one GPU node and measure resident bytes and tokens/s (<$20k).
prior_art: BitDelta (2024) fused 1-bit deltas; DeltaZip compressed-delta serving; S-LoRA/Punica for adapters. From memory.

key_insight: Variants do form lineages (base, domain, tenant). Deltas against a parent are smaller in magnitude, so per-row scales fit more tightly and fidelity may improve.
killer_doubt: A sign delta costs 1 bit/weight whatever its magnitude, with ~1 bit of entropy. So the tree saves zero memory over flat BitDelta and adds depth-d dequant-adds per GEMM.
decisive_experiment: Simulation only (<$10k): build a 3-level tree of Llama fine-tunes and compare raw bytes, entropy-coded size and perplexity for flat versus tree 1-bit deltas.
prior_art: BitDelta (2024); DeltaZip; delta chains in model hubs (ZipNN). Tree-structured 1-bit serving: none found. From memory.

key_insight: Dictionaries matter because small blocks compress poorly. With a 4 KB random-access granule, a trained dictionary lifts zstd from ~2-3x to ~5-8x on logs and JSON.
killer_doubt: 10-20x needs whole-file or columnar (CLP-style) compression, not 4 KB random access. Log/JSON stores are a few percent of DRAM, and software zstd dictionaries already do this.
decisive_experiment: Software trace study (<$30k): zstd with trained dictionaries at 1, 4 and 64 KB blocks on real log, trace and JSON stores. Plot ratio against decode latency. Build hardware only if the 4 KB ratio is >=8x.
prior_art: zstd dictionary training (Meta); IBM z15 on-chip zEDC; Intel IAA; YScope CLP log compression; CXL compressed-memory controllers. From memory.

key_insight: The physics is valid: compute a shared prefix's KV once and fetch it over RDMA, and repeated prefixes stop costing prefill FLOPs and pinned HBM.
killer_doubt: It already ships. Llama-70B KV is ~320 KB/token, so a 4k-token prefix is ~1.3 GB, ~26 ms at 50 GB/s RDMA. It wins only for long, popular prefixes.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Benchmark LMCache or Mooncake against recompute on a shared-prefix chat trace and measure TTFT and HBM per GPU (<$20k).
prior_art: Mooncake (Kimi, FAST 2025); LMCache; CachedAttention (ATC 2024); NVIDIA Dynamo KV offload; SGLang RadixAttention. From memory.

key_insight: Compression cuts DRAM per device only if buyers count compressed GB. An audited trace-based rating (like EPA mileage) turns zram's ~2.5-3x ratio into a number procurement can use.
killer_doubt: Phones already ship zram and laptops ship OS compression. The real limit is CPU and latency on incompressible apps, so a certified 1.6x likely cuts DRAM 10-20%, not 25-40%.
decisive_experiment: Build the benchmark (<$300k): replay 50 phone, laptop and server traces under zram/zswap on 8 GB versus 12 GB devices and publish effective GB at fixed p95 latency. Ask two OEMs whether they would down-spec.
prior_art: Apple's '8 GB ~ 16 GB' claim; Samsung RAM Plus; Windows memory compression; SPEC/MLPerf-style benchmarks. Certification: none found. From memory.

key_insight: RS(8,2) costs 1.25x against 3x for replication, saving ~58% of DRAM for replicated in-memory data. The GF math is cheap: ISA-L encodes at ~5-10 GB/s per core.
killer_doubt: Hydra and Carbink already do erasure-coded far memory. Degraded reads fan out to 8 servers (~10-20 us tail), and replicated in-memory stores are a few percent of DRAM.
decisive_experiment: Nothing is needed. Run Hydra's open code against 3x replication on a memcached trace and measure DRAM per object and p99 with one node failed (<$20k).
prior_art: EC-Cache (OSDI 2016); Cocytus (FAST 2016); Hydra (NSDI 2022); Carbink (OSDI 2022, Google). From memory.

key_insight: At 1% BER, protecting 64 B lines needs ~27-44% ECC overhead (finite-length bound). An annealed index map that makes flips nearly harmless could replace that overhead for VQ weights.
killer_doubt: A 16-bit codebook index flips with 15% probability at 1% BER, and pseudo-Gray maps have historically given ~2-4 dB, not 5-10x. The cheap 1%-BER cell does not exist yet.
decisive_experiment: Simulation (<$20k): AQLM 2-bit Llama-3-8B with 1% iid and row-clustered flips injected. Compare random, annealed and MSB-protected index maps on perplexity and MMLU.
prior_art: Pseudo-Gray coding (Zeger-Gersho 1990); channel-optimized VQ (Farvardin 1990); EDEN approximate DRAM for DNNs (MICRO 2019). From memory.

key_insight: A relaxed-BER SKU with system ECC sells bits that are scrapped today. It is also the market vehicle for ECC-paid cells: raw BER 1e-4 already halves capacitor height (C0 N-62).
killer_doubt: Reject-die failures are clustered (rows, columns, banks, periphery), not iid, and makers already sell eTT/UTT grades. Net new supply may be only ~2-5% of bits.
decisive_experiment: Buy ~1,000 UTT/eTT DDR4/DDR5 dies and map BER against refresh and temperature with DRAM Bender (FPGA). Measure clustering. Run cross-die LDPC plus refetch for KV and weights (~$250k).
prior_art: eTT/UTT gray-market DRAM grades; Flikker (ASPLOS 2011); EDEN (MICRO 2019); HRM Par+R (DSN 2014, via search snippet). A formal AI-grade SKU: none found.

key_insight: KV is the largest inference memory consumer, and attention averages over many tokens, so moderate iid noise in values is genuinely tolerable.
killer_doubt: An int4 code cannot leave its range, so clamping does nothing. At 1% BER, flip noise is 10x quantization noise (~2.3 effective bits), and capping softmax breaks one-hot retrieval heads.
decisive_experiment: Simulation (<$20k): KIVI int4 KV on Llama-3-8B with 1% injected flips. Compare clamp+cap, ECC on the MSB plane only (flip noise 2.5x quantization noise), and no protection, on RULER and LongBench.
prior_art: Ranger range restriction (2021); EDEN (MICRO 2019); unequal error protection of DNN bit-planes; KIVI/KVQuant 2-4-bit KV. From memory.

key_insight: Eviction robustness can be trained in. Models never shown missing context collapse under H2O-style eviction, while trained ones should degrade gracefully.
killer_doubt: Evicted information is gone, so needle recall falls roughly with the drop rate. MLA (~93% KV cut), DMC (4-8x) and Gemma-3 local:global (~5x) already beat the claimed 2-4x.
decisive_experiment: Continue pretraining a 1B model on ~20B tokens with 30-70% stochastic eviction (~$60k of GPU time). Compare against DMC at equal KV budget on RULER and LongBench.
prior_art: DMC (NVIDIA 2024); MLA (DeepSeek-V2); DuoAttention; Gemma-3 local/global layers; H2O, SnapKV, TOVA eviction. From memory.

key_insight: Clean data has a master copy, so detection plus refetch can stand in for correction. That also makes non-iid failures (dead rows, VRT bursts) survivable.
killer_doubt: At p=1e-2 and 4 KB, the finite-length bound gives 12.3% overhead at FER 1e-15 and 10.9% at 1e-6. That saves ~1.4 points, and a 64 B read pulls 4 KB.
decisive_experiment: Fold this into I-10425. On DRAM Bender data, compare a CRC+refetch tier with an LDPC tier for page cache, measuring refetch rate, decoder pJ/bit and p99 page latency (<$50k extra).
prior_art: HRM Par+R (Luo et al., DSN 2014): parity detection plus a clean-copy reload from disk (via search snippet); cache designs that refetch clean lines.
